title: Unique compatible internal-Hom section lifts on affine opens
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent ideal, and $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ coherent modules [pqf-def-coherent]. Write $\mathcal P_n=\mathcal P/\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal P$ and $q_n^{\mathcal P}$ for the quotient projections and use the canonical transition maps [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Put $\mathcal H=\mathcal Hom(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Suppose $e_n:\mathcal H_n\to\mathcal Hom(\mathcal G_n,\mathcal F_n)$ satisfies $q_n^{\mathcal H}$ followed by $e_n$ and precomposition by $q_n^{\mathcal G}$ equals postcomposition by $q_n^{\mathcal F}$. Let $t_n:\mathcal G_n\to\mathcal F_n$ commute with every transition map. For any affine open $U\subseteq X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], there is exactly one family $s_n\in\mathcal H_n(U)$ commuting with all transition maps and satisfying $e_n(U)(s_n)=t_n|_U$ as a section of $\mathcal Hom(\mathcal G_n,\mathcal F_n)(U)$ for every $n\geq0$. Only sections over $U$ are asserted, not a global section or compatibility between distinct opens.

proof.text: Apply the affine tensor dictionary to obtain rho, the completed-ring-linear evaluation beta, its pure-tensor formula, and the equation characterizing each compatible family t.

The affine section ring A is Noetherian. Coherence gives quasi-coherence and finite type of G. Use the existing proved Scheme.Modules.isFiniteType_over helper from FinitePushforwardCoherent, available through a proof-only import all, to restrict finite type to the slice over U, and use the affine finite-type criterion to obtain a finite A-module N=G(U). Module.finitePresentation_of_finite makes N finitely presented.

Mathlib supplies flatness of B=AdicCompletion J A and the base-change linear equivalence theta=(Module.FinitePresentation.isBaseChange_map A N M B).equiv. For b tensor h, B-linearity and b tensor h=b smul (1 tensor h) reduce equality beta=theta to the dictionary generator formula and IsBaseChange.equiv_tmul. TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.ext proves their equality; therefore beta is bijective.

Let v represent t under the dictionary. Surjectivity of beta gives w with beta(w)=v; put s=rho.symm(w). The dictionary iff proves all evaluation equations for s. If s′ also satisfies them, beta(rho(s′))=beta(rho(s)); injectivity of beta and then of rho gives s′=s.
